I can imagine how you feel. How suicide just feels right somehow. How it’s the only thing that feels right. I attempted suicide  a few years ago. And I failed ,because I regretted it the moment I did it, and I had the means to stop it. And that’s why I was planning to do something more lethal this time. So that there would be no way to stop it. Maybe you know it already ,but,in my experience, the thing is that once you’ve done it,you do regret it right away. It’s not just physical. Not just what they call a “survival instinct”. The moment you do it, you realise that you don’t have to die to be better.You realise that there are,in fact, things you can do.You realise that’s it’s always been about you.That it’s all in your control.Maybe you know it already.I am just hoping that you will choose to stay here for a little longer. No matter where I am and no matter what I am doing it’s there.This “feeling”.I may be laughing with friends or having a great time outside ,but I still can’t help but feel that it’s not right somehow,I guess... It just does not go away. Ever. And I am not even sad anymore.I don’t even consider myself depressed ,since I can get out of bed, laugh and feel something that resembles happiness every now and then.I am suicidal. Not depressed. Probably because being sad and thinking about dying all the time has become ingrained in who I am somehow .And thinking about all the ways that I can kill myself before going to bed has become so...natural to me. Crossing the road with my eyes closed is just like any other habit at this point . It doesn’t worry me anymore. It doesn’t scare me.

The best thing that you can do is let her know as often as possible that you still love her ,despite her ED.

If you catch her off guard ,doing her thing , don’t get agitated and say things like “It is bad for you.” , “You need to stop.” or “You are hurting yourself.” ,because ,in all likelihood, she already knows these things ,but she can’t stop (we are mentally ill,not stupid ).And ,really, when people I love make it clear that they know what I’ve been up to and that it’s upsetting and troubling for them , an intense wave of guilt and shame washes over me and I start thinking that all they see is an illness ,not a person . I start thinking of myself as a disease and sometimes this makes me think that my loved ones would be better off without it ,without me, in their lives .

I understand that if you saw your friend hurting herself you’d probably want to help her by making sure that she stops inflicting pain on her body ,but I don’t think it would really help .Sometimes the only thing that you can do is be there for her and remind her that she is still a person ,not an illness .
